column8: What did the pilot ask for on the primary control axis? The mouse IS the stick on this aircraft (computeMouseAim swings the virtual cursor by this delta) and until v2 no mouse quantity was recorded at all -- 31 fields answering what the AIRCRAFT did, none answering what the PILOT asked. This is the EFFECTIVE delta the aim law consumed: after the _G.__evcSynthDelta instrument add and after the release-guard zeroing, so an F4 sweep frame and a release-guard frame both record the value the maths actually used, and a replay that REPLACES the delta reproduces the frame exactly. 0.00 on a frame where computeMouseAim did not run (mouse-aim off, free-look, or right-click zoom) -- a true statement about the aim path, not a claim that the pilot's hand was still; keyMask bit256 distinguishes free-look.

column8: Which keys did the pilot hold? The second half of what-the-pilot-asked. Bits 1-32 are the QWEASD flight axes read from the kb table's RAW +-1/0 targets -- the same values CS-1's aimGate reads at :5083, so this field also witnesses WHY mouse-aim was muted on a given frame, which no field could say before. Bits 64/128 are the flap-throttle keys, the only other input that reaches the plant (:5103-5104) and previously invisible: flapThrottle is sticky, so a tape could show thrust with nothing on it explaining where the thrust came from. Bit256 records free-look, under which the mouse drives the camera instead of the aim path and ords 32/33 correctly read 0.
